svg.title: 02 / HydroSense system flowchart
svg.desc: Water filtration and ESP32 operation | Based on thesis V23, pp. 60-62 and Appendix I | See Flowchart 01 for app navigation
svg.text: Water filtration and ESP32 operation | Based on thesis V23, pp. 60-62 and Appendix I | See Flowchart 01 for app navigation
Initialize ESP32, sensors, LCD and relays;
Read app mode and pump commands
when Firebase is ready; read ToF tank
level, float switches and leak sensor
Apply latest Pump A / Pump B commands
FS1 down + FS2 down: A enabled; B OFF
FS1 up + FS2 down: A enabled; B ON
FS1 up + FS2 up: A OFF; B ON
FS1 down + FS2 up: A OFF; B OFF
If A enabled: cycle 30 s ON / 60 s OFF
Otherwise keep A OFF; apply B state
Water route: biofilter media and the downstream five-stage treatment are distinct assemblies (thesis pp. 61-62).
Control polling and pump / safety checks: 500 ms
pH, processed TDS and turbidity: about 1 s
Local LCD: 2 s; pump status: on change
App writes mode and pump commands to Firebase.
App reads sensor values and actual relay state.
Filter model is trained on generated data and
uses measured Pump B runtime for live estimates.
A = intake pump; B = filter-feed pump
apply in both AUTO and MANUAL.
Timing and branch details follow Appendix I code. The prose on p. 62 differs on telemetry timing and the full-tank inequality.
Firmware uses a 5-second telemetry interval and a >=100% full-tank stop. Local safety logic continues without a cloud connection.
Sources: physical route, pp. 61-62; existing overview, p. 60; controller constants and safety / AUTO branches, pp. 166-177.
